description: alarms.v2 §2.4, §3: the packed Alarm of alarms.v2.json (core §7.6). Computed twice by two scripts of the text's drafter that share no code, kept out of the repository, and never blessed. `schema` is the profile's packed document. `layouts`: the type -> its layout form, the sha256 of its JCS bytes, its tag, and its shortest and longest record in bits, before the pad. `writes`: the deployment `epoch` in seconds (0 where none is given) and a value in core §7.6's JSON reading (`rule` and `argument` a number or "not_available", `at` in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, `key` the alert key as an integer, `severity` null for the escape, an absent optional field no member) -> the record's `bits` before the pad, the `pad` and the bytes in `hex`; with `stamp`, the owner's own stamp of that put (<run>/<seq>, the run in 4 lowercase hexadecimal digits for a 16-bit run and 8 for a 32-bit run, the seq in decimal), also the put's `payload`: CH (form 0, the stamp's width bit, the type's tag), the run, the seq, the record; or {refused: token}. The writer's tokens are the core's packed/vectors.json's (`missing`, a field not given; `unknown`, a member the type does not have; `value`, a value of the wrong JSON type or a name not declared; `range`, a value with no code), then this text's, for a value the core writes: `key_with_rule` (`key` given under a table's rule), `key_missing` (no `key` under not_available) and `by_words_fields` (`labels` given, or an `argument` other than not_available, under not_available). An accepted write reads back to its value. `reads`: CH's `tag`, the record's bytes and the epoch -> {value} or {undecodable: token}, the first of: core §7.6's refusals (`tag`; then `length`, the record ends before a bit the layout needs; then `length`, a byte after the pad; `pad`, a pad bit set), then `key_with_rule` and `key_missing`. No field has an unused code, so no record is refused `code`; the layout ends at its marker, so none is refused `extension`: a marker read as 1 ends the reading, the rest a later text's. A reader ignores `labels` and `argument` under not_available, and the value shows them as read.

schema.description: alarms.v2's standard packed schema (spec/profiles/alarms/v2.md, section 3; core section 7.6). The standard contract alarms.v2.toml lists this file and types its resource alarms/{slot} by it. An alarm's slot is its key's last chunk, never a field. Its rule and its labels are numbers that the service's own table names (the annotation alarms.rules, section 4), or its rule is not_available and its words are on words/{slot} (section 2.4).

Alarm.description: state alarms/{slot}: one alarm's record. 35 bits, 5 bytes, with no optional field; 67 bits, 9 bytes, with its time; 91 bits, 12 bytes, with its labels too; 131 bits, 17 bytes, for an alarm named by words, with its time and its key.

fields.name: state
fields.description: Whether the alarm fires. The record says the state, never the sample's kind, the heartbeat's bit or its live count.

fields.name: severity
fields.description: In that order. The escape is a severity a later text names: a reader of this one reads it as no severity known.

fields.name: rule
fields.description: The rule's index in the service's table. not_available for an alarm no table names: its words are on words/{slot}, and its record carries key.

fields.name: at
fields.description: When the alarm's latest transition happened (a raise, an escalation or a resolve), on the owner's clock, in whole seconds. It is the acknowledgement identity. Absent while that clock reads no instant the deployment epoch codes.

fields.name: labels
fields.description: The codes of the rule's labels, in the table's order, the first the most significant, as one integer. Present exactly where the rule declares a label.

fields.name: argument
fields.description: The rule's own number: the reading that changes while the condition holds. It reads as the rule's minimum plus this code times its resolution. not_available where the rule declares none, or the reading has no code.

fields.name: key
fields.description: The alert key, as the 64 bits of its hash. Present exactly where rule is not_available. It counts nothing: a counter is the one kind that holds 64 bits.
